lesson.theme: Explain forgotten errands and completed tasks
lesson.small: A friend asks what small task you finished recently. Give one truthful sentence and one detail.
lesson.scenario: A friend asks whether you completed errands yesterday. Explain what you meant to do, what you forgot and what you managed to finish. Ask about tomorrow's plans. The friend changes one plan after your first answer.
lesson.writing: Write four sentences in present simple, past simple, present continuous and future simple. Change two to questions and two to negatives.
lesson.note: Everyday scenario; reviews from Days 27 and 20.
lesson.noticing: I meant to buy milk yesterday, but I forgot to stop at the shop. I managed to buy bread. I changed my mind about dinner. I'm planning to shop tomorrow, but I'll play it by ear.
lesson.story: Describe an errand you intended to finish and what happened.
lesson.recovery: Describe the missing word in simple English and finish the sentence.
lesson.writingCheck: I buy bread every week. I bought bread yesterday. I am buying bread now. I will buy bread tomorrow. Did you buy bread yesterday? I did not buy milk.

ambiguity.sentence: I finally got the errands out of the way before lunch.
ambiguity.gist_question: Were the errands completed before lunch?
ambiguity.plain_english: Finished so they no longer need attention.
ambiguity.context_clue: Finally and before lunch suggest completion.

foundation.title: Questions and negatives across four tenses
foundation.rule: Use do or does for present simple, did for past simple, am/is/are for continuous and will for future. Use the base verb after do, does, did and will.
